ai_note: Biopharma oncology/metabolic/ADC business; no AI exposure in revenue, cost base, or valuation narrative.
why: Hansoh is compounding on a structural mix-shift, not a cycle: innovative medicines (led by Ameile/aumolertinib's expanding NSCLC indications and XINYUE's new autoimmune approvals) have risen from a generics-heavy base to ~85% of revenue, and a validated out-licensing platform (GSK, Regeneron, Roche, Glenmark, Avere deals since mid-2025, including the October 2026 Roche ADC deal worth up to ~$15bn in milestones) is layering a second, higher-margin revenue stream on top. Returns are excellent (ROIC 89.7%, 3yr avg 54.9%) and the balance sheet is net cash (~RMB33bn, D/E 0.0).
watch: Interim growth trend: H1 FY2026 revenue was +11.7% YoY, below the 13/11/10% base-case product-sales path and the model's own 'slowing' flag -- a further deceleration toward single digits would end the acceleration thesis

NRDL renewal cycles for Ameile, Hansoh Xinfu, XINYUE, Fulaimei, Hengmu and Saint Luolai -- industry-wide price cuts have averaged ~60% on newly negotiated oncology drugs; any cut of that magnitude on a top product would hit the ~66%-of-revenue oncology franchise directly
Price vs. valuation: shares are HK$31.86 against IV HK$27.27 (-14.4% upside) and the base-case entry price is HK$16.84 -- a near 50% discount to today's price, so this is not a buy at current levels

Licensing/collaboration income cadence: FY2025 collaboration revenue (~RMB2.1bn, ~14% of revenue) is lumpy and milestone-contingent; a gap year with no new deal signed, or a partner (GSK/Roche/Regeneron/Avere) stumbling in trials, would remove a chunk of the growth premium baked into the bull case
next_catalyst: FY2026 full-year results (historically reported around March, per FY2025 results cadence); near-term watch also includes any further out-licensing deal announcements following the October 2026 Roche ADC agreement
